finding: Land now refuses a real fix after `git rebase --ignore-date` or `--reset-author-date` onto a newer feature tip, because those options give every replayed commit a new author date, so its authorship no longer matches the commit the branch made. The patch-id rule this delta removed accepted that rebase, because the patch is unchanged. The refusal says no commit was made on the branch, which sends the developer the wrong way.
why: The delta's own docstring says authorship is what a rebase keeps: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:646 "Commit id -> author name, e-mail and date: what a rebase, squash or fixup keeps."; ship.py:657 says a replayed commit counts when it has the "same author and author date". Round 8 judged a false refusal of a rebased fix to be high (JOURNAL.md new line 169: "matching by patch id refused a fix whose patch a rebase changed").
fix: Count a replayed commit when its author name and e-mail match a made commit AND either its author date or its patch id matches (compute the patch id once per made and per replayed commit). Or, at minimum, name the date-resetting rebase options in the refusal reason and pin the behaviour with a test.
evidence: ship.py:684 `made |= {c for c, key in _authorship(cwd, replayed).items() if key in own}`; ship.py:650 `"--format=%H%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%ad"`. Probe <scratch>/r9ds-probe/test_probe9.py (fix commit, feature moved, sleep 1.2 s, `git rebase -q <opt> origin/feat/export`), output <scratch>/r9ds-probe/out9.txt: `=== K --reset-author-date` -> `result={'step': 'land', 'status': 'refused', 'reason': 'none of the 2 commits past the Base commit b5c504a... was made on fix/bug-export-drops-row, so land would ship no fix'}`; `=== L --ignore-date` -> same refusal; `=== J --committer-date-is-author-date` -> `'status': 'done'`.

finding: No test pins that `own` takes in commits made between rebases. A mutant that reads authorship only at the first `(finish)` entry passes all 21 rebase and land-kind tests, and with it land refuses a fix committed after one rebase and replayed by a second, with the false reason that no commit was made on the branch.
why: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:656-657 "a commit a later rebase or rebasing pull replayed from one of those (same author and author date)"; every land test with a `(finish)` entry has at most one made commit after the last `(finish)` that precedes it, so a second refresh is never needed.
fix: Add a land test: checkout -B at the feature tip, stranger pushes later1.txt, fetch, `git rebase -q origin/{FEATURE}` (assert the last reflog entry has `(finish)`), commit fix.txt, stranger pushes later2.txt, fetch, rebase again; assert land `done`, remote tip == HEAD, entries == [push line]. Probe-verified: passes on e854cc40, fails on the refresh-once mutant.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros) / mutation probe: survived mutant on a delta line
finding: No test pins the author half of the key. A mutant keyed on the author date alone (`--format=%H%x00%ad`) passes all 21 rebase and land-kind tests, and with it a stranger's commit authored in the same second as the branch's fix counts as the fix after a rebase replays it, so land no longer refuses a branch that dropped its fix.
why: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:646 "Commit id -> author name, e-mail and date" and ship.py:657-658 "a replayed commit the branch never made counts for nothing". The only test separating own from foreign replayed commits by identity (`replays_only_commits_made_elsewhere`) uses a same-author commit with a different date, so only the date half is exercised.
fix: Add a land test: checkout -B at the feature tip, commit fix.txt, stranger commits later.txt with `--date=<fix's raw author date>` and pushes, fetch, `git reset -q --hard origin/{FEATURE}`, `git rebase -q --force-rebase {start}`; assert land refused with "was made on". Probe-verified: passes on e854cc40, fails on the date-only mutant.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:650 `"--format=%H%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%ad", check=False, stdin="\n".join(shas) + "\n").stdout`. By contrast name_only, email_only and drop_date are each killed by both params of test_fast_forward_land_refuses_a_rebase_that_replays_only_commits_made_elsewhere.

finding: The new merge test rebases onto `origin/{FEATURE}`, so the rebase result equals its `onto` commit and the replayed range is empty; the authorship match never runs. The test passes even when every replayed commit counts as made, so it cannot fail for the rule its name states.
why: The test asserts land is refused because the stranger commit was not made on the branch (scripts/tests/test_ship.py:1103 `assert result["status"] == "refused" and "was made on" in result["reason"], result`), but the only code that could wrongly count that commit, ship.py:683-684, gets an empty `rev-list {onto}..{sha}`. The round-8 proposal this test answers named `git rebase -q {start}` (docs/afk/small-lane/plan/review/0007-ship-script-2cfd96b-r8.findings.json, r-002 fix).
fix: Rebase onto `start` instead (`git(repo, "rebase", "-q", start)`), so the stranger commit falls in the replayed range, and keep the asserts. Probe-verified: that variant passes on e854cc40 and fails on the count-every mutant.

'how': 'found'}`).

finding: A replayed commit that the branch never made now counts as land's fix if it has the same author name, e-mail and author second as any commit the branch made. The removed patch-id rule refused this case because the content differed. Agents that commit under one shared identity, or a setup that pins GIT_AUTHOR_DATE, make this collision reachable.
why: ship.py:657-658 (delta): "a replayed commit the branch never made counts for nothing."
fix: Add a content signal to the authorship match, for example the patch id or the subject as an alternative to the date (as in delta-sweep-001), so that one author second cannot stand for a different commit. Then add a test like test_fast_forward_land_refuses_a_rebase_that_replays_only_commits_made_elsewhere, but with a branch commit made first under the same author date.
evidence: Probe H2 in <scratch>/r9ds-probe/test_probe9.py: commit fix.txt on the Diagnosis branch with GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=1790000000 +0000; commit elsewhere.txt on local branch `wip` with the same identity and date; `git reset --hard wip`; feature moves; `git rebase origin/feat/export`. out9.txt `=== H2 own commit from other branch, SAME second` -> `'status': 'done', 'push': 'feat/export@6d6807aa...'`. The same flow 1.2 s apart (`=== H ...other second`) -> `'status': 'refused'`.

finding: The delta now accepts a rebase whose conflict was resolved with `git rebase --continue`, but a sibling path still refuses. If the developer resolves the conflict with `git commit` and then continues, or adds or splits a commit at an `edit` stop, the new commit gets a new author date, and only HEAD's reflog records it, not the branch's. Land then refuses the fix.
why: Round 8's remediation target (JOURNAL.md new line 169): "matching by patch id refused a fix whose patch a rebase changed"; ship.py:656-657 says a commit that a later rebase replayed from a made commit counts.
fix: Also read `git reflog show HEAD` and count `commit`/`commit (amend)` entries that fall between this branch's `rebase (start)` and its `rebase (finish): returning to refs/heads/{branch}` as made. Or say in the refusal reason that commits made during a rebase stop are not counted.
evidence: Probe C2 (conflict, `git add`, `git commit --no-edit`, `git rebase --continue`): out9.txt `=== C2 conflict resolved by git commit then --continue` -> `'status': 'refused'`. Its HEAD reflog: `a5b0745 rebase (finish): returning to refs/heads/fix/bug-export-drops-row` / `a5b0745 commit: add fix.txt` / `ef41bba rebase (start): checkout origin/feat/export`. In its log, a5b0745's author date is 1793212277, a new date, not the made commit's. Probe N (split at an edit stop): `=== N split commit at an edit stop` -> `'status': 'refused'`.

criterion: Mutation probe: survived mutant on a delta line
finding: No test pins `--date=raw`. Dropping it passes all 21 rebase and land-kind tests, and with it a repository that sets `log.date=short` reads every same-day commit by the developer as the same key, so a rebase that replays only the developer's own work from another branch counts as a fix.
why: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:657-658 "a replayed commit the branch never made counts for nothing"; `%ad` follows the `log.date` config unless `--date` is given, and the tests never set `log.date`.
fix: Add `git(repo, "config", "log.date", "short")` as the first line of a copy of test_fast_forward_land_refuses_a_rebase_that_replays_only_commits_made_elsewhere (or parametrize it). Probe-verified: passes on e854cc40, fails with `--date=raw` removed.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:649 `out = _git(cwd, "log", "--no-walk=unsorted", "--stdin", "--date=raw",`. Mutant drop_raw: <scratch>/r9tv-mut/drop_raw.out `21 passed, 90 deselected`.
